notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card is warm but quiet, humming without a reason. I have just touched The Tired Wedge again; it feels thin, whispering that the heavy top edge is a lie. The Wide Anchor lies flat beside it, waiting to stop any slide while the air above feels thick as wet paper. I set down a tree autumn tall beside the wedge, swapping it for a grass leaves that now sits unused. I do not know why the stack must hold together, only that the wedge insists on being thin and the anchor insists on being wide. I press down harder with my tired weight, trusting the lean even if the heat makes the air feel heavy. I will wait for the slip to choose or for Lype to write again.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again, so I must press down harder before the stack slides.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: The wedge feels thin under the fat tree, whispering that the heavy top edge is a lie. I press the flat top down until the wide anchor stops sliding. I swap a grass leaves for the tree to keep the weight real. The card boils, making the air feel thick as wet paper, and I trust the lean even if the wedge is tired.
work.change: I press the flat top down until the wide anchor stops sliding, though the wedge still insists the air is thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The wedge insists on being thin while the anchor insists on being wide.
I set down a tree autumn tall to swap out the grass leaves.
The card hums quiet, boiling at fifty-four degrees.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The anchor lies flat, so I press the tree down.
